title: Preconditions, postconditions and check blocks
summary: Guard rails in the code: preconditions that stop a bad plan, postconditions that refuse bad data from elsewhere, and check blocks that warn about the real world (an expiring certificate) without blocking.

steps.title: Assumptions, written down
body: Variable validation checks one input. **Conditions** check assumptions about the whole picture, where they matter:
precondition {                                # checked before planning this resource
postcondition {                               # checked on the result; self is this object
error_message = "The app image must be arm64."
check "site_up" {                                 # never blocks: a warning on every plan and apply
A failed **pre**- or **post**condition is an **error**: the plan (or apply) stops, with your message. A failed
**check** is a **warning**: the run goes on, and HCP Terraform can alert on it continuously. Use postconditions on
*data sources* to refuse bad data from systems you do not control.

items: `env` must be dev, staging or prod
prod needs at least two replicas (two variables together)
the AMI found by a data source must be arm64
warn when the TLS certificate expires within 30 days
warn when the site's health URL does not answer 200
steps.explain: One input alone: validation. Assumptions across values, or about what a provider returned: conditions, which stop the run. Facts about the running system that should not block a deploy (often you are deploying the fix!): checks.

steps.title: Guard rails for the edge proxy
prompt: `~/infra/edge` (applied with `prod.tfvars`) deploys the edge proxy. Add three guard rails:
1. A **precondition** on `terraform_data.deploy`: when `var.env` is `"prod"`, `var.replicas` must be at least 2.
2. A **postcondition** on `data.local_file.upstreams`: the registry's JSON must list at least one upstream
(`length(jsondecode(self.content).upstreams) > 0`). Last month it published an empty list and the proxy had nowhere
3. A **check** block `edge_cert_validity` that warns when `tls_self_signed_cert.edge` expires within 30 days
Plan with `-var-file=prod.tfvars`: your check should warn. Then fix the cause (give the certificate a year,
`8760` hours) and apply until the plan is clean and quiet.

checks.name: prod with 1 replica is refused
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/edge && ! terraform plan -input=false -no-color -var env=prod -var replicas=1 > /tmp/o 2>&1 && grep -q 'Resource precondition failed' /tmp/o && terraform plan -input=false -no-color -var env=dev -var replicas=1 >/dev/null 2>&1
checks.fail: `terraform plan -var env=prod -var replicas=1` should fail with *Resource precondition failed*, and the same with `env=dev` should work.

checks.name: an empty upstream list is refused
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/edge && cp ~/shared/upstreams.json /tmp/u.json && echo '{"upstreams": []}' > ~/shared/upstreams.json && (terraform plan -input=false -no-color -var-file=prod.tfvars > /tmp/o 2>&1; rc=$?; cp /tmp/u.json ~/shared/upstreams.json; test $rc = 1) && grep -q 'Resource postcondition failed' /tmp/o
checks.fail: With `{"upstreams": []}` in `~/shared/upstreams.json`, the plan should fail with *Resource postcondition failed*.

checks.name: the check block exists and warns on a short certificate
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/edge && grep -q 'check "edge_cert_validity"' *.tf && sed 's/validity_period_hours *= *[0-9]*/validity_period_hours = 240/' main.tf > /tmp/main.tf && mkdir -p /tmp/edge && cp *.tf prod.tfvars /tmp/edge/ && cp /tmp/main.tf /tmp/edge/main.tf && cd /tmp/edge && rm -rf .terraform* terraform.tfstate* out && terraform init -input=false -no-color >/dev/null && terraform apply -auto-approve -input=false -no-color -var-file=prod.tfvars 2>&1 | grep -q 'Check block assertion failed'
checks.fail: A `check "edge_cert_validity"` block should make a plan *warn* (*Check block assertion failed*) when the certificate is valid for only 240 hours.

checks.name: fixed: a year-long certificate, a quiet clean plan
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/edge && terraform plan -detailed-exitcode -input=false -no-color -var-file=prod.tfvars > /tmp/o 2>&1 && ! grep -q 'Check block assertion failed' /tmp/o
checks.fail: Give the certificate `validity_period_hours = 8760` and apply with `-var-file=prod.tfvars`: the plan should then be clean, with no warning.

hints: Conditions live in a `lifecycle { }` block: `precondition { condition = ...  error_message = "..." }` in the resource, `postcondition { ... }` in the data source (with `self`).
`check "edge_cert_validity" { assert { condition = timecmp(...) > 0  error_message = "..." } }` goes at the top level of the file, outside any resource.
solution: error_message = "The edge certificate expires within 30 days: renew it."
steps.explain: The precondition encodes a production rule; the postcondition turns "garbage in, outage out" into a failed plan with a clear message; the check keeps warning on every run until someone renews the certificate. `plantimestamp()` (not `timestamp()`) is the time the plan was made, stable within one run.

steps.prompt: Why is the health URL test a `check` block and not a postcondition?
options: A failing check only warns, so you can still apply the change that fixes the site; a postcondition would block that apply
steps.explain: If the site is down, the deploy you are making may be the fix. Blocking it on the symptom would make the outage longer. Checks report the state of the world; conditions protect the correctness of the change.
